Bhagavad Gita, Chapter 2, Verse 5

“Better to live on alms in this world than to kill these great-souled teachers. If I killed them, even though they seek worldly gain, every pleasure I tasted here would be smeared with their blood.”

Arjuna imagines the victory concretely and finds it unbearable — food, wealth, kingship all stained. The image of blood-smeared enjoyments is his own, and shows a conscience working in vivid pictures.
